newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain threatens Cuba ban after tourist imprisoned.
newsitem.headline: Spain threatens Cuba ban after tourist imprisoned.

text.p: Spain, angered by the imprisonment of a Spanish tourist in Cuba, threatened on Wednesday to issue a travel ban and take other measures against the island nation to demand his release.

"This situation is intolerable," Foreign Minister Abel Matutes told state radio. "Spain is going to use all of its resources and those of its European partners to get his immediate release and return to Spain."

The row, the latest in a series this year between Cuba and its former colonial power, developed when Spanish tourist Jesus Martin was arrested and put in prison after a small traffic accident a month ago.

Martin, speaking to state radio from Cuba, said he had been asked to pay for damages and had been imprisoned when he could not immediately come up with the money. He has been held since then without being able to speak to a lawyer or see a judge.
Matutes said Spain was studying a possible travel ban to Cuba because of its "absolute lack of judicial controls".
"We are studying the possibility, given this lack of guarantees, to recommend that Spanish citizens not travel to Cuba," he said.
